abstract: Dallas Fed economists Samuel Dodini and Tucker Smith (Sept 22, 2026) link Texas administrative education and earnings records to a college-major measure of exposure to GenAI automation (Anthropic's task-based Claude usage measure, mapped to majors through pre-ChatGPT Lightcast postings). After ChatGPT's release, graduates from more-exposed majors saw a 1.7-percentage-point relative decline in the probability of finding employment in Texas within a year of graduating, per 10-percentage-point higher share of automatable tasks, and those who found jobs saw first-year earnings fall by about 5% from 2021 to 2024 relative to less-exposed majors. May 2024 graduates from more-exposed majors were 1.4 pp more likely to enroll in graduate school, mostly in the same field; master's holders in exposed fields saw similar relative earnings declines, suggesting limited returns to formal upskilling. Undergraduate enrollment fell 4.8% between fall 2024 and fall 2025 per 10-pp higher automatable-task share. The authors conclude GenAI caused declines in employment and earnings for new graduates with automatable skill sets.
keyFindings: 1.7-percentage-point relative decline in the probability of Texas employment within a year of graduating, per 10-pp higher automatable-task share (post-ChatGPT cohorts vs May 2021 baseline).
First-year earnings for more-exposed majors fell about 5% from 2021 to 2024 relative to less-exposed majors (chart data: -5.38, 95% band -6.68 to -4.07 for the 2024 cohort).
May 2024 graduates from majors with 10-pp higher exposure were 1.4 pp more likely to enroll in graduate school; two-thirds of returning 2024 CS graduates chose a CS graduate program.
Master's holders in more-exposed fields saw relative earnings declines similar to bachelor's graduates.
Texas four-year undergraduate enrollment fell 4.8% between fall 2024 and fall 2025 per 10-pp higher automatable-task share.
methodology: Event study on Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board and Texas Workforce Commission records for graduates of Texas public four-year universities; employment and nominal earnings over the first four quarters after graduation; cohorts relative to May 2021 graduates. Major exposure = average Anthropic task-automation share of occupations whose Lightcast job ads (2018Q1–2022Q3) request that field of study.
qualifiers: Tier 1: Federal Reserve Bank research, consistent with the repo's treatment of other Dallas Fed Economics posts; not peer reviewed. Outcomes observe only employment in Texas (UI records), so graduates who leave the state count as not employed. Earnings are nominal, though the relative comparison nets out common inflation. Earnings effects condition on finding a Texas job and may reflect selection. Exposure is task capability from Claude usage, not firm adoption. Effects are scaled per 10 pp of automatable-task share, not a most- vs least-exposed contrast. The authors attribute causation ('GenAI caused declines'); the design is a pre/post exposure comparison with stable pre-trends.
